header.running_head: The services of Women in Jihaad

blocks.text: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) and other women of the Ansaar would march with Rasulullaah ﷺ on military expeditions. Their function was to provide water and tend to the wounded.[^1]
The Services of Hadhrat Rubayyi Bint Mu'awwidh (RA), Hadhrat Ummu Atiyya (RA) and Hadhrat Layla Ghifaariyya (RA) in Jihaad

Hadhrat Rubayyi Bint Mu'awwidh (RA) reports that when they (women) were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on military expeditions, they would provide water (for the soldiers), treat the wounded and retrieve the bodies of the dead.[^2] Another narration of Bukhari quotes that she said, "We (women) would proceed on military expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ where we would fetch water for the people, serve them and return the dead and wounded to Madinah (when the battlefield was close to Madinah)."[^3]

Hadhrat Ummu Atiyya (RA) who was from the Ansaar says, "I accompanied (the army of) Rasulullaah ﷺ on seven military expeditions. I would stay behind in their camp preparing food for them, nursing their wounded and tending to those with various diseases."[^4]
Hadhrat Layla Ghifaariyya (RA) narrates, "I used to proceed on military expeditions with Rasulullaah ﷺ to nurse the wounded."[^5]
The Services of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) and Hadhrat Ummu Saleet (RA) During the Battle of Uhud

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "When the Muslims suffered some defeat during the Battle of Uhud and were unable to stay with Rasulullaah ﷺ, I saw Aa'isha (RA) the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA) and Ummu Sulaym (RA) with their shawls folded high (to allow free movement). I could see their ankle bracelets as they ran with water bags." Another narration states that the two of them were carrying water bags on their backs, emptying the water into the mouths of the wounded and then returning to refill them. They then again returned to empty the water into the mouths of the injured.[^6]
